Following the idx_bdb235c6 Zero Trust principle of least privilege idx_dc2e04ff access, GSA uses Role-Based Access
Control (RBAC) to manage administrative access. Microsoft Entra ID offers several built-in
roles that can be assigned to administrators who manage GSA. They are as follows:
Security Administrator: This role grants permissions to perform specific tasks like
configuring remote networks, setting up security profiles, viewing traffic logs etc. This
role cannot configure Private Access.
Global Secure Access Administrator: This is also a limited role and can perform tasks
such as configuring remote networks, managing traffic forwarding profiles, viewing
traffic logs etc. This role cannot configure Private Access or create and manage
Conditional Access policies. It also cannot manage user and group assignments.
Conditional Access Administrator: This role is required to create and manage
Conditional Access policies for GSA.
Application Administrator: This role can configure Private Access, private network
connectors, application segments and enterprise applications.
Global Secure Access Log Reader: This role is intended for staff that need read-only
access to traffic logs. They cannot make changes to the environment; however, they can
view detailed GSA traffic logs including session, connection and transaction data. They
can also review alerts and reports.
Security Reader and Global Reader: These roles have read-only access to GSA except
for traffic logs.
To perform idx_c0f1d700 tasks in Microsoft Entra, administrators need to have the Global Secure Access
Administrator and the relevant role assigned. For example, if administrators need to create
Conditional Access policies, they should be assigned both the Conditional Access
Administrator and the Global Secure Access Administrator roles.
GSA offers useful dashboards that provide visualization of data across Microsoft Entra Internet
Access and Private Access. This helps administrators understand the number of devices that
are using GSA in the network, the usage patterns, most used destinations, cross-tenant activity
patterns and more. Administrators with the Global Secure Access Administrator idx_b943a297 role can view
this dashboard in the Microsoft Entra admin center by navigating to Global Secure Access |
Dashboard.
Before proceeding with Microsoft Entra Internet Access, let's explore some key concepts of
GSA.

traffic goes over the internet. Traffic forwarding profiles are used to decide which traffic goes
through the client and which over the internet. This client is available for Windows, macOS,

Virtual Private Network (VPN). Over time, the number of devices that need access to

Chapter 14 488
Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) cannot meet these demands. Moreover, some
idx_780827cc branch offices have physical firewalls which require maintenance by an IT team. Placing an IT
team in each branch office is expensive.
GSA helps idx_e0498cfa connect these remote offices to the corporate idx_02271e08 network over an Internet Protocol
Security (IPSec) tunnel. This tunnel is established between a customer premises equipment
(CPE) and the idx_5c257b0f nearest GSA PoP. This eliminates the need for each client in the remote office to
have a VPN or GSA client installed. Once the IPSec tunnel is established, traffic forwarding
profiles route designated traffic from the remote office over the tunnel, while other traffic is
routed over the internet. GSA provides secure network connectivity for employees in remote
offices without needing to route traffic to their headquarters.
Following are the prerequisites for setting up a remote network:
A Global Secure Access Administrator role
CPE must support the following:
IPSec
GCMEAES128, GCMAES192, or GCMAES256 algorithms for Internet Key
Exchange (IKE) phase 2 negotiation
Internet Key Exchange Version 2 (IKEv2)
Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)
CPE must use RouteBased VPN with any-to-any traffic selectors
CPE must initiate the connection using Responder modes
Remote networks in GSA can be created in the Microsoft Entra admin center using the steps
below.
Sign in to https://entra.microsoft.com as a Global Secure Access Administrator.
Navigate to Global Secure Access | Connect | Remote networks.
In the right pane, click Create remote network.
On the Basics page, enter the name of the remote network and select the region. This is
the Microsoft PoP that your remote network will connect to. Select the region closest to
your location. Click Next: Connectivity.
On the Connectivity page, enter the device links for the remote network. These can be
added after the remote network has been created. Device type, IP address, and BGP
address are required. Once done, click Next: Traffic profiles.
On the Traffic profiles page, choose if you want to route internet traffic or Microsoft
365 traffic. Click Next: Review + create.

Traffic forwarding enables organizations to configure the type of traffic to be routed over

Traffic profiles apply to the user who is logged into the device.
If there is no user logged in, then a profile applies only if it is assigned to all users. For

Multiple idx_6f457924 users logging in to the same device simultaneously is not supported.
Group-based assignments are only supported for Security groups and Microsoft 365
groups whose SecurityEnabled is set to True.
Nested groups are not supported.

In addition to the above profiles, a Microsoft Entra traffic profile handles all authentication
and identity-related traffic for Microsoft Entra services. This profile ensures that identity traffic
is always acquired and protected regardless of license assignment. Following are the key
features of this profile.
Always on: This profile is automatically enabled whenever any of the other traffic

No assignment requirement: This profile is automatically included in any active
traffic forwarding profile and does not require any explicit user or branch assignment.
Coverage: This idx_b02ab650 profile covers a defined set of Fully Qualified Domain Names (FQDN)
and IP ranges of the Microsoft Entra services. All traffic for these destinations is
automatically acquired by this profile and routed through the GSA service.
This idx_e6fd8935 profile is Microsoft-managed and is not visible in the portal.
Access controls
GSA can idx_4706757e apply several access controls to the idx_d5cd130a traffic being routed through it. Let's explore some
of them.
Universal Conditional Access
GSA is integrated with Conditional Access policies and can apply policies to secure traffic
profiles. Controls idx_26f03ed9 like MFA, compliant device or idx_109a5b1e risk-level can be applied to network traffic.
These policies can be applied to all traffic acquired by Microsoft Entra Private Access or
Microsoft Entra Internet Access profiles. This functionality helps protect applications that
don't support modern authentication. Conditional Access policies can be targeted to traffic
profiles and not specific applications. This is done by selecting All internet resources with
Global Secure Access under Target resources while creating the Conditional Access policy.
Compliant network check
The integration idx_be29b48b between GSA and Conditional idx_797a452e Access can prevent malicious access to
applications using several conditions, such as device compliance and location. GSA introduces
the compliant network check, which ensures that users are connecting through the GSA
client installed on their devices or through configured remote networks. This ensures that
traffic for protected resources is flowing through the GSA service and that clients are compliant
with the security policies enforced by the Conditional Access policies.
Compliant network check reduces the risk of token theft and token replay attacks.

493 Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Source IP restoration
Cloud idx_daf5a62a security layers like SSE, SWG, ZTNA, CASB, etc. typically idx_c0c6524f mask the user's true IP. The
destination service sees only the cloud proxy's IP. This creates several problems, such as:
Conditional Access based on trusted IPs fails because Entra ID cannot see the user's
actual egress IP.
Audit logs lose fidelity, showing the proxy's IP instead of the user's real location.
Location-based risk signals degrade, making it harder to detect anomalies.
Legacy apps relying on IP allowlists break, because the "source IP" is no longer the
corporate or expected IP.
Source IP restoration in GSA restores the user's original client IP address when their traffic
passes through a cloud-based network proxy or SSE service. This allows Microsoft Entra ID and
Microsoft Graph to evaluate network-based policies and logs using the true client IP address.
Source IP restoration is enabled for all tenants created after June 2025. To explicitly enable or
disable this feature, turn Enable Conditional Access Signaling for Microsoft Entra ID on or
off as explained in the Compliant network check section.
This allows Entra ID to receive the public egress source IP address of the user.
Understanding Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Microsoft Entra Internet Access is a cloud-delivered identity-centric Secure Web Gateway
(SWG) designed idx_384410de to safeguard organizational resources as users access the internet and cloud-
based applications from any location or device. By leveraging idx_3b7bb612 identity-aware controls, it
provides secure browsing, enforces access policies, and helps prevent data leaks at the network
edge. Microsoft Entra Internet Access integrates seamlessly with Microsoft's SSE strategy,
combining web protection, threat defense, and visibility into user activity. The solution
empowers organizations to enable remote and hybrid work while maintaining robust security
standards and centralized management, ensuring users stay protected no matter where or how
they connect. The following are some key features of Microsoft Entra Internet Access.
It can acquire network traffic using traffic forwarding profiles.
It records detailed traffic logs for internet traffic and provides detailed dashboards that
show relationships between users, devices and endpoints.
It integrates with Conditional Access policies to apply network security policies using
context-aware vectors like user, device, device compliance, location, and risk.

categories or FQDNs.

Internet Access profile
To use Microsoft Entra Internet Access, you must first enable the Internet access profile. Refer
to Figure 14.3. Once enabled, traffic to the public internet, except for the Microsoft traffic
profile, will be idx_9830b3e8 forwarded to the service idx_b631800a through the GSA client or the remote network. This
profile includes a list of regular expressions for FQDNs and IP Addresses representing the
public internet. It includes the following Internet access policies:
Custom bypass: Administrators can define traffic that must be excluded from being
routed to the service. Traffic for the destinations listed under this policy will not be
acquired by the profile. Organizations usually exclude traffic for their VPN endpoints,
private IP idx_945d5309 ranges and networks that use a network Access Control List (ACL). To add
rules to this policy, click on Add rule as shown in Figure 14.6. You can add a FQDN, IP,
IP Subnet or IP Range. Once a rule is added it takes 15-20 minutes to appear on the
client computer.
Default bypass: This policy contains predefined internet traffic that the profile does
not acquire, like private IP ranges. The rules in this policy cannot be changed.
Microsoft traffic bypass: This policy lists all traffic that can be acquired by the
Microsoft traffic profile. This traffic is bypassed by the Internet access profile and is
acquired by the Microsoft traffic profile when it is enabled. The rules in this policy
cannot be changed.
Default acquire: This policy defines traffic that is always acquired by the profile. All
internet idx_845e4807 traffic on ports 80, 443 over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is
included in this policy. This policy has the lowest priority and is processed after all
bypass rules are processed. The rules in this policy cannot be changed.

Security profiles
Security idx_9fc059aa profiles help organize policies like web idx_cb189561 content filtering policy, TLS inspection policy,
threat intelligence policy and more. They can be linked to Conditional Access policies to make
them user and context aware. One security profile can have multiple web filtering policies, TLS
inspection policies, threat protection policies, and more. One security profile can be linked to
multiple Conditional Access policies. For example, you could have a security profile for the
finance department containing all policies specific to the finance department. This security
profile can then be applied to all users in the finance department using a Conditional Access
policy. Within a security profile, policies are enforced based on priority of numbers: 100 is the
highest priority and 65000 is the lowest priority. When a security profile is linked to a
Conditional Access policy, if multiple Conditional Access policies match, all matching security
profiles are processed as per priority ordering.

Edge. For idx_5bae3cda unencrypted HTTP traffic, Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is used. For idx_00dafdbb HTTPS
traffic encrypted using Transport Layer Security (TLS), Server Name Indication (SNI) is

Configuring Transport Layer Security inspection
Transport Layer Security (TLS) protects idx_36316f26 privacy by encrypting idx_699a6844 the data transmitted between
a user's device and the destination server. This means that idx_82f92e8e even if someone intercepts the
network traffic, they cannot read the contents without the proper decryption keys. TLS also
ensures the authenticity of the server, helping users confirm they are communicating with the
intended party and not an imposter. As a result, sensitive information such as login
credentials, personal data, and business communications remains confidential during transit.
However, this also enables malicious traffic to be hidden behind encryption. TLS inspection is
the process of intercepting, decrypting, and analyzing encrypted internet traffic. This enables
organizations to inspect data for threats or policy violations while maintaining security. After
inspection, the data is re-encrypted and sent to its destination, ensuring privacy and
compliance with security standards.
TLS inspection in GSA decrypts HTTPS traffic and applies security controls like web content
filtering. It uses a two-tier intermediate certificate method to issue leaf certificates that are
dynamically idx_df13b030 generated. These leaf certificates are used to decrypt traffic and protect against
threats that hide behind encryption.
To configure idx_b5d455d8 TLS inspection in GSA, ensure that idx_676a6716 there is an existing Public Key Infrastructure
(PKI) service available idx_a0aa678d to sign the Certificate Signing Request (CSR) and to generate a
certificate for TLS inspection. The following are the steps to create a CSR and upload a signed
certificate:
Sign in to https://entra.microsoft.com as a Global Secure Access Administrator.
Navigate to Global Secure Access | Secure | TLS inspection policies.
In the right pane, click on TLS inspection settings and click Create certificate.
In the flyout pane, enter the following details and click Create CSR once done.
Certificate name: This name appears in the browser when the certificate is
viewed. It must be unique, with no spaces, and should not be more than 12
characters in length.
Common name: Any name that identifies the certificate.
Organization name: Any name that identifies the organization.
The CSR is created and saved to your default downloads folder. This CSR must be
signed by your PKI service and saved in .pem format.
Click on Upload certificate and upload the .pem files and click Upload signed
certificate as shown below.

Configuring threat intelligence
Threat intelligence refers to the process of collecting, analyzing, and applying information
about current idx_23e0b26d and emerging cyber threats. It helps organizations protect their users from
accessing malicious websites based on real-time threat information, ultimately strengthening
overall security posture. Threat intelligence in Microsoft Entra Internet Access enables
organizations to block traffic based on domain and URL indicators. It uses Microsoft and non-

File policies in GSA support idx_1fab6d54 network content filtering to help safeguard idx_b372d0e8 against data leakage
into generative AI applications and other internet destinations. Using this, organizations can
extend data protection capabilities to network traffic in real time. Administrators can discover

This solution idx_4be82dbc integrates with Microsoft Purview's data classification service to provide Data
Loss Prevention (DLP) at the network layer. This combination creates a DLP service at the

Microsoft Entra Internet Access for Microsoft
Services
This feature idx_043af8fc improves security and enhances performance for Microsoft 365 services. The

It enables users to connect directly to Microsoft services using traffic forwarding

Entra ID applications integrated with Conditional Access.

be enabled in Global Secure Access.
Microsoft traffic profile
This profile idx_5b37f0bb acquires traffic for Microsoft 365 services like Exchange Online, SharePoint Online,
Microsoft Teams and other Microsoft apps. This profile ensures best performance for these
services and simplifies configuration of the rules that govern traffic acquisition. Microsoft
traffic policies (Figure 14.3) consists of rules that include the Destination Type, Protocol,
Ports, Category, and Action. These are derived from the master Microsoft 365 IP and FQDN
list. Rules are grouped by workload. You can use the Enable/Disable check box to indicate if
the traffic for that group should be bypassed or acquired. When a group is enabled, the GSA
client or remote network will acquire all traffic for that workload. Individual rules can be
configured for an enabled group. For each rule, if Action is set to Forward, traffic for the
specified destination will route through the GSA client or Remote network. Setting a rule to
Bypass will send that traffic over the client's network routing path to egress to the internet.

Microsoft Entra Private Access
In today's increasingly hybrid and remote working environments, organizations face
significant challenges in providing secure access to private, internal applications. Traditional
Virtual Private Network (VPN) solutions, while widely used, are often complex to manage,
may introduce idx_65eadb7c vulnerabilities, and do not always provide granular, identity-based controls.
Microsoft Entra Private Access addresses these modern security needs by enabling secure,
seamless connectivity to private applications—regardless of whether users are working from a
corporate office, home, or on the move.
The need for Microsoft Entra Private Access arises from the shift toward zero trust security
principles. Rather than relying on a trusted network perimeter, organizations now require
robust mechanisms to ensure that only authenticated and authorized users can access
sensitive resources. With the idx_6f951dbd proliferation of cloud adoption and bring-your-own-device
(BYOD) policies, the risk of unauthorized access and data breaches increases. Microsoft Entra
Private Access integrates with Microsoft's identity services, allowing for policy-driven access
controls, real-time monitoring, and adaptive security responses based on user context and risk.
Furthermore, it simplifies the user experience by eliminating the need for cumbersome VPN
connections while offering IT teams centralized visibility and governance.
In this chapter, we will cover:
Introduction to Microsoft Entra Private Access
Private Access for domain controllers
Application usage analysis
Logs and monitoring
•

Understanding Microsoft Entra Private Access
Microsoft Entra Private Access is a modern solution designed to provide secure, seamless
access to idx_0e225a76 private, internal applications for users in any location. Built to support today's
remote and hybrid work environments, it eliminates the complexity of traditional VPNs and
enables organizations to adopt a Zero Trust security model. Users connect idx_68a29a90 to internal
applications and resources using the Global Secure Access (GSA) client installed on their
devices. By integrating with Microsoft Entra's identity services, Private Access ensures that
only authenticated and authorized users can reach sensitive resources, using adaptive policy
controls and real-time monitoring. This approach simplifies remote access for end users while
granting IT teams centralized visibility, governance, and the ability to enforce robust security
measures across the enterprise.
The Private Access traffic profile determines the traffic to be routed through the GSA client.
This profile is enabled in the Microsoft Entra Admin center by navigating to Global Secure
Access | Connect | Traffic forwarding and switching the toggle to on as shown in the

There are two ways to configure access to private resources that you want to make accessible
through the GSA service.
Quick Access
Quick Access idx_c22c2f24 is a group of Fully Qualified Domain Names (FQDNs) and IP addresses that the
organization wants to secure. When idx_7025af05 quick access is configured for the first time, a new
enterprise application is created and is automatically configured to work with Private Access.
Employees can then access the specified applications using the GSA client. The following figure
shows a Quick Access configuration:

Quick Access idx_fa3852e6 can be used as a transition state toward a Zero Trust posture.
Organizations looking to replace their VPN can start by using Quick Access to rapidly secure all
private network traffic through Microsoft's global backbone with identity-based controls. Once
traffic patterns are understood and apps are discovered, they can transition to per-app access,
applying granular Zero Trust policies to each application, reducing lateral movement, and fully
eliminating traditional VPN dependencies.
Creating a private network connector group
The first idx_187f1187 step is to configure idx_990e0e91 a connector group with at least one active Microsoft Entra Private
Access connector. Each connector group can handle traffic for specific applications. A
connector group operates as a single unit. Therefore, it is recommended to configure at least
two connectors in each connector group for high availability and load balancing. Connectors
523 Microsoft Entra Private Access
can be added or removed at any time. Location based connector groups can reduce latency for
large organizations that have applications in many regions by having each connector group
serve local applications.
Connectors idx_571658f5 are lightweight idx_517b73b3 agents installed on a Windows Server in a private network and
facilitate outbound connection to the GSA service. This Windows Server must have access to
the on-premises applications. Users connect to the GSA service which uses these connectors to
route traffic to the on-premises applications.

An account with the Application Administrator role assigned.

4.5 527 Microsoft Entra Private Access
Per-app access
Organizations often have varying security needs for private resources, such as different
Conditional idx_ba3006a9 Access policies for specific idx_f8e1705f users or limited-time access. Microsoft Entra Private
Access enables per-app controls using Global Secure Access apps, allowing fine-grained access
management for various private applications. Multiple Global Secure Access apps can be
created to address distinct app segments. The following figure shows per-app access
architecture:
Figure 15.6: Per-app access architecture
Configuring per-app access involves creating the Global Secure Access apps and assigning
users and groups to the app. Before continuing, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:
You must have the Global Secure Access Administrator and the Application
Administrator roles assigned.
Create a connector group with at least one active private network connector. This is
explained in the section, Creating a private network connector group earlier in this
chapter.
Now you can proceed with creating the Global Secure Access app.
Creating a Global Secure Access app
Fine-grained access to private app segments is provided using Global Secure Access apps.
Unlike idx_d64484a9 Quick Access, where the idx_9c3226af enterprise application is automatically created when Quick
Access is configured, for per-app access the application must be manually created. The
following are the steps to create a Global Secure Access app:
Sign in to https://entra.microsoft.com as a Global Secure Access Administrator
and Application Administrator.
•
•
1.
